st_a_climbers_look.description: I climbed redwoods for a living back in Humboldt County, in California. The tallest tree on Earth was a redwood called Hyperion, and the great sequoia on the slopes here would make Hyperion look like a sapling. I'm not climbing anything that big until I know how it's standing. Go and look at the base for cracks, and then cross the slopes and look at which way it would fall. It's on the Sequoia Slopes, north of the vale.
st_a_climbers_look.accept_text: Kick the roots at the base as you go round. A sound root rings, and a rotten one thuds.

st_a_name_on_the_post.description: You turn the charm over in your hand. It's a Bloodhoof hunting charm you took off one of the risen stalkers, braided hide and a carved bead, and there's a name worked into the bead. Whoever wore it was a hunter of Mulgore, and somebody on Sun Rock will know whose it was. Kuna Ashhorn keeps the hunters' post on the south-east tower at Sun Rock Retreat. She knew every hunter in Mulgore, and she'll know this one.
st_a_name_on_the_post.accept_text: You tuck the charm away gently. The braid is coming loose, and you don't want to lose the bead.

st_ash_for_brill.description: I've got ash from the wraiths and ash from the thing that made them, and I want both of them in the hands of the apothecaries at Brill. They'll know what to do with it. It's better if you don't know. I've sealed it in lead, because I'm not a monster. Brill's in Tirisfal Glades, near the Undercity, and Assistant Grael will take it from you.
st_ash_for_brill.accept_text: Don't drop it, and don't shake it. I mean both of those quite seriously.

st_ash_that_walks.description: The forest on the Blowdown came through with the mountain three years ago, and it didn't burn. It was knocked flat in a single breath and buried in ash, and its spirits never had time to leave. Now the Ash Drifters walk the burn, and I believe they're what's left of the trees, trying to remember what they were. They walk the open burn north and west of here. I'd like them put to rest, gently if you can.
st_ash_that_walks.accept_text: If one stops and stands still near you, let it. Some of them are nearly done remembering.
st_ash_that_walks.turn_in_text:
The burn's quieter. I can hear the wind on it again, and nothing else.

They didn't ask for what happened to them.

st_aspen_answer.description: Hoka wrote three pages to his sister, and then he asked me to add a fourth. It says the Aspen has room for anyone from Sun Rock who wants to come south. It also says the Aspen's hunters will stand with Sun Rock if the Rim ever breaks, and I meant every word of that. I'd like it carried back by the same hands that brought the first letter. Take it to Halona Stillwater at Sun Rock Retreat, and tell her the Aspen meant what it wrote.
st_aspen_answer.accept_text: Give her time to read it before you go. She'll want to send something back.

st_beetles_in_the_bark.description: I walk the fog under the redwoods that came through with the mountain, and the bark beetles have never been this bad. They bore into the giants and lay their eggs, and a tree that big dies so slowly that nobody notices until it's too late. I want them cut back before they reach the oldest trees. They're thickest in Greatwood Vale, below the camp. Stand still and you'll hear them chewing.
st_beetles_in_the_bark.accept_text: Burn the bark where you find the eggs. Crushing them only spreads them.

st_blasting_caps.description: The Venture Co. blasters are clearing the Blowdown with powder, and they're not careful about it. One of their charges shook the whole mesa last week and took a corner off the inn. I want their blasting caps, and I want their yard foremen dealt with, because without both of them nothing goes bang. They work the Venture Salvage Yard, north-west of here. Carry the caps very carefully, and I'm being serious.
st_blasting_caps.accept_text: Pack them in sawdust if you can find any. The yard's got plenty lying about.

st_broadpaw.description: Broadpaw is the black bear the Standing Grove belongs to. He's never bothered the hunters before, but the cougars have pushed him out of his den, and now he takes his temper out on anybody in the trees. I'm sorry for the bear, truly. But he's hurt two of my hunters, and he has to go. You'll find him deep in the grove, bigger than any bear you've seen.
st_broadpaw.accept_text: He's deep in the Standing Grove, and he'll charge. Don't be standing where you were when he does.

st_carrion_from_the_rim.description: I watch the Mulgore Rim from the south-east tower, every night. The carrion birds that roost on the Rim fly into Mulgore after dark and come back in the morning. What they carry in their beaks shouldn't be carried anywhere, and they've started dropping it near the camp. The Rim is in the south-east corner of Stonetalon, where the light goes strange. Kill them before they bring any more of Mulgore to Sun Rock.
st_carrion_from_the_rim.accept_text: Don't stand under them when they fall. Whatever they're carrying comes down too.

st_cartel_paperwork.description: Somebody signed those blasting caps out of a Cartel warehouse, and I want to know who. The Cartel's warehouse ledgers for this side of the world are kept by Factor Weezel in Booty Bay, because Booty Bay never throws anything away. I've written down every stamp number off the caps. Booty Bay is at the bottom of Stranglethorn, in the Eastern Kingdoms. Weezel will tell you he's busy, so wait for him anyway.
st_cartel_paperwork.accept_text: Don't let him charge you for the wait, because he'll try.

st_cores_of_ash.description: The ash drifters on the Blowdown are made of the same ash the mountain threw, and they pack it down tight in their middles like a core sample. If I can read their layers, I can tell how long the mountain rested between eruptions. That tells me how long we've got before the next one. They walk all over the Blowdown, so break them open and bring me what's in the middle. It'll be warm, which is good, because it means it's fresh.
st_cores_of_ash.accept_text: Wrap each core in its own cloth. If two touch, the layers smear.

st_cougar_stew.description: I feed everybody on Sun Rock, and the elk are running thin this season. Cougar makes a good stew if you cook it long enough, and the ridge cougars have been eating very well on the Blowdown. I'd rather they fed us than we fed them. They hunt all over the Blowdown and in the Standing Grove. Bring me their flanks, and I'll do the cooking.
st_cougar_stew.accept_text: Cut from the hindquarter. The front's all sinew, and it never softens.

st_cougars_in_the_grove.description: The Ridge Cougars have learned that Sun Rock's hunters bring meat home through the grove. Two of my people were jumped last week, and one of them won't walk right again. I want the cougars taught that the hunters bite back. They hunt the Standing Grove and the rocks round it, and they hunt from above. I've lost count of the times I've told the young ones that, and I'll keep saying it until they listen.
st_cougars_in_the_grove.accept_text: Look up before you look ahead. They'll be waiting on the rocks.

st_fallen_not_felled.description: I won't touch a living giant, and nobody on Sun Rock will. But the Blowdown is full of trees that came through already down, and redbark from a fallen tree is every bit as good as redbark from a standing one. I need logs for the new lodge. Cut them where they lie, all over Stonetalon. You'll need woodcutting, and I'll teach you if you haven't got it.
st_fallen_not_felled.accept_text: Leave the ones with moss on the north side. Those are still settling, and they split badly.
st_fallen_not_felled.turn_in_text:
These are good, straight logs. These will hold a roof up for a hundred years.

Now they need milling.

st_fireweed_and_amber.description: I've heard that the Eldest Sequoia's sap runs as living amber inside the trunk, and that it heals burns better than anything that grows outside. The Venture Co. has been tapping it to sell, and the living sap that pools in the galleries carries the amber. I want some before they sell all of it. The children here burn themselves on the cooking fires every week. Go in at the tree's foot, and take friends, because it's dangerous in there.
st_fireweed_and_amber.accept_text: Go into the Eldest Sequoia from the door at its foot. The living sap moves through the lower galleries.
st_fireweed_and_amber.turn_in_text:
Look at the light in it. That light comes from the tree itself.

I'll make a salve that'll keep the children's burns from scarring.

st_for_the_society.description: I need a second opinion, and the only Forsaken apothecary I trust on this side of the world is Dellwyn Voss, at Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Voss has written four reports about something in the mere water there that won't die properly. I think it might be the same thing as the Rim. I've packed the samples in ice, and I need them carried across the sea. Don't open the box, and I do mean that.
st_for_the_society.accept_text: Hammerfall's in the Arathi Highlands, in the Eastern Kingdoms. Don't open the box.

st_gnawheart.description: The bark beetles have a mother, and I've found where she's been laying. She's inside a giant in Greatwood Vale that's hollow now from root to crown. I call her Gnawheart, because that's what she does. The beetles won't stop coming while she lives. She's bigger than a kodo, so bring friends.
st_gnawheart.accept_text: Don't let her get behind you. She comes out of the walls of that trunk.
st_gnawheart.turn_in_text:
That's the end of the eggs, and there won't be beetles like that again.

The Mistwalkers will remember this. Take what you like.

st_grael_writes_back.description: I've written back to Rennick. The ash is exactly what Brill wanted, and we'd like more. There's also a warning on the second page. The Royal Apothecary Society has heard about his work, and they'd like a word with him. I didn't say which word.
st_grael_writes_back.accept_text: Take this back to Rennick. He'll be pleased, until he reads the second page.
st_grael_writes_back.turn_in_text:
They want more ash, and the Society wants a word, which is just wonderful.

Well, you've been very good to an old corpse. Take this, and don't tell the tauren where it came from.

st_grandfather_burl.description: Grandfather Burl is the oldest of the redwood ancients. He woke when the Venture Co. cut his neighbour, and he's been walking the Sequoia Slopes ever since, tearing out anything that moves, Mistwalkers included. I loved him. I knew him for three years, which is nothing to a tree, and I still say I loved him. He walks round the foot of the great sequoia, so go and give him rest.
st_grandfather_burl.accept_text: He's slow and he's very, very strong, so go together.
st_grandfather_burl.turn_in_text:
He's rooted again. I watched him do it. He picked a spot in the sun and put his roots down and stopped.

That's the end I wanted for him.

st_grimtotem_intent.description: Orgrimmar wants to know whether the Grimtotem mean to take Sun Rock or only to frighten it, and I can't tell them from up here. Their compound is south of the Blowdown. Get close enough to see what they're building inside the walls. If their brutes come at you, make an example of them, so they know they've been seen. Then come back and tell me everything.
st_grimtotem_intent.accept_text: Count the ladders while you're there. That number tells me more than anything else.
st_grimtotem_intent.turn_in_text:
They're building siege ladders.

Then they've stopped threatening and started planning. I'll write to Orgrimmar tonight.

st_ground_zero.description: I studied volcanoes in Washington State before the Integration, and I'm almost sure the mountain above Sun Rock is something like Mount St. Helens. The Blowdown looks exactly like what happened there in 1980, right down to the way the trees are lying. I need to see the middle of the blast and the edge of the salvage yard, but I'm not much use with a weapon. Go and stand where the blast was strongest, out in the middle of the Blowdown, and then look over the yard. Tell me which way the trees are lying.
st_ground_zero.accept_text: Look at the stumps as much as the trunks. The stumps don't lie about which way the blast came.
st_ground_zero.turn_in_text:
They're lying away from the peak in a fan, and stripped of their bark on one side. It's St. Helens. It's exactly St. Helens.

Which means that mountain isn't finished, and somebody should probably tell the tauren.

st_hargol_bloodhorn.description: Hargol Bloodhorn leads the Grimtotem in Stonetalon. The fire was his idea, and so are the ladders. I don't think there'll be a siege without him, and Orgrimmar has said it would rather there wasn't one. I'm asking you to make sure there isn't. He's in the middle of the Grimtotem Compound with his best people round him, so take yours.
st_hargol_bloodhorn.accept_text: Watch the ladders on your way in. They've built more since I last looked.

st_harpies_on_the_crag.description: The Windshear harpies have nested on the crag north of the Blowdown for as long as anyone remembers. Since the mountain blew, they've been coming down on Sun Rock's supply lines and taking whatever they can carry. I've lost two carts this month, and a driver who didn't let go fast enough. Windshear Crag is the high ground north-east of here, past the Blowdown. Push the harpies and their talons back up the crag where they belong.
st_harpies_on_the_crag.accept_text: Go for the talons first if you can. The others lose their nerve without them.

st_hides_for_the_cold.description: Winter on a mesa is cold, and a bear hide is the warmest thing a tauren can sleep under. The refugees came here with nothing, and some of them are sleeping on bare stone. Black bear from the Standing Grove or greatwood bear from the redwoods in the West, it doesn't matter which. I've tanned hides since I was a calf, and I've never had so many people waiting on me. Bring me the hides, and I'll tan them for the refugees' beds.
st_hides_for_the_cold.accept_text: Skin them whole if you can. A hide in pieces makes a cold bed.

st_hides_for_the_lodge.description: I've got more people on Sun Rock than I've got roofs. The refugees who got out when Thunder Bluff fell are sleeping under the sky, and the wind off the Blowdown has started to bite at night. The old ones are beginning to cough. Elk hide makes a good tent, and the grey elk graze all over the burn below us. The bull elk keep to the Standing Grove in the south-west. Bring me their hides and I'll see them stitched before the cold sets in.
st_hides_for_the_lodge.accept_text: Take the hides off whole, without nicks. A hole in a tent lets the whole wind in.
st_hides_for_the_lodge.turn_in_text:
These will keep a family dry.

A tent's a small thing, but it's a long way better than sleeping under the sky.

st_hulks_on_the_peak.description: The Basalt Hulks and the Peak Sky Serpents have started coming down off the peak to my sampling sites, and I've run out of patience and nearly out of sites. I'd do it myself, but I'm an alchemist, and I've never been any use in a fight. They're all up on Stonetalon Peak, north of here, at the top of the mountain. Clear them off the high ground round the crater. Then I can get back to work without looking over my shoulder.
st_hulks_on_the_peak.accept_text: The serpents dive from the sun. Keep it at your back if you can.

st_into_the_ashvent.description: The Ashvent is a lava tube on the flank of the peak, and the heat at the bottom of it shouldn't be there. Something called Magmacore sits on the last of the molten rock and keeps it from cooling. As long as it does, the whole mountain stays warm, and the next eruption gets closer. I can't go down there myself, but you can. The tube opens on the peak's north flank, and Magmacore sits at the very bottom.
st_into_the_ashvent.accept_text: Bring heat-proof friends. Nobody else will last long at the bottom.

st_iron_under_the_burn.description: There's good iron on Stonetalon now that the trees aren't sitting on top of it. Sun Rock needs spearheads, hinges and nails, and I can't make any of them without ore. The refugees are building homes with rope and hope, and that won't last a winter. Iron turns up all over the Blowdown and the slopes in the West. Bring me what you can dig, and I'll teach you mining if you don't know it.
st_iron_under_the_burn.accept_text: Bring the dark ore if you see any. It's poorer, but it's easier to work.
st_iron_under_the_burn.turn_in_text:
That's good ore, clean, and plenty of it.

Sun Rock will have nails by the morning. Take this with you. It's the last thing I made from Thunder Bluff iron.

st_kingsblood_for_the_sick.description: Half the children on Sun Rock have a cough from the ash, and it's getting worse as the nights get colder. I know an old Mulgore remedy that uses kingsblood, and kingsblood grows on Stonetalon if you know where to look. I can't leave the camp, because the sick need me here. It grows on the slopes all over Stonetalon, and you'll need a little herbalism to pick it. Bring me what you find.
st_kingsblood_for_the_sick.accept_text: Pick the leaves, not the root. It grows back faster that way, and we'll need it again.
st_kingsblood_for_the_sick.turn_in_text:
That's enough for every child in the camp, and some for the grown-ups too.

You've no idea how good it'll feel to hear them sleep through the night.

st_letter_to_the_aspen.description: My brother Hoka left Thunder Bluff a different way when it fell, south toward the mountains. I heard he reached the Aspen Wilderness, where the Keeper of the old lift still waits for a cable that doesn't come back. I've written him a letter, and I don't know if he's alive, but I want it sent anyway. The Aspen Wilderness is south, past the Barrens, where the mountains came through, and Keeper Nalu Stillgrass keeps the old lift there. Ask her about a tauren named Hoka, and don't believe he's gone until you've asked.
st_letter_to_the_aspen.accept_text: If he's there, tell him I kept his drum. He'll know which one.

st_matron_shrieka.description: Matron Shrieka is the oldest of the Windshear wind witches. She makes every fetish on the crag, and she sends every raid down onto our road. Driving her off won't do it, because she'll only come back and start again. I want her gone for good. She keeps the highest nest on Windshear Crag, and you'll hear her long before you see her.
st_matron_shrieka.accept_text: Plug your ears if you can. Her screaming is half the fight.

st_meat_for_the_rock.description: I hunted Mulgore my whole life, and now I hunt for a mesa full of people who lost everything. There aren't enough hunters, and there are a great many mouths. The bull elk in the Standing Grove are fat, and the grove is thick enough to sneak up on them. It's in the south-west, among the trees the blast missed. Bring me venison, as much as you can carry.
st_meat_for_the_rock.accept_text: The Standing Grove's in the south-west. The bull elk graze between the trees. Come in from downwind.

st_old_greyhide.description: There's an elk on the Blowdown that should have died when the mountain blew. Old Greyhide was standing in the blast and walked out of it, and he hasn't been right since. He leads the grey elk round and round the place where the forest used to be, and the herd follows him. They won't scatter while he lives, and they need to scatter to find new grazing, and I've asked the spirits for another way and been given none. You'll find him in the middle of the Blowdown, huge and grey, with ash in his coat to the skin and the herd round him.
st_old_greyhide.accept_text: Be quick with him. He's been walking in a circle long enough.

st_orders_in_ash.turn_in_text:
They meant to burn the Blowdown again with Sun Rock in the middle of it. It was clever, and it very nearly worked.

You found this by luck and acted on it fast. Orgrimmar will hear about you.

st_planks_for_the_lodge.description: I've got the logs, and now I need planks. I'd like you to mill them yourself at my bench, because once you've cut the boards for a lodge, you'll never look at one the same way again. It's slow work, and it teaches you patience. Straight, even planks are all I ask. Mind your thumbs.
st_planks_for_the_lodge.accept_text: Plane with the grain, never against it. Redbark splinters like it's angry.

st_rest_for_the_eldest.description: The heart is clean now, but the Eldest's spirit isn't at peace. I've been listening at the foot of the tree for three nights, and what I hear from the crown is rage. It's been bored and tapped and climbed on for so long that it lashes out at anything that moves. The tree will go on standing whatever happens. The spirit just needs to sleep, so climb to the crown and give it rest.
st_rest_for_the_eldest.accept_text: Climb the trunk and out onto the crown. The Eldest waits at the very top. Bring your best people.

st_road_west.description: I've got a dispatch for Orgrimmar's envoy at Sun Rock Retreat, up in Stonetalon. I don't trust the Grimtotem with it, I don't trust the harpies with it, and frankly I don't trust you much either. But you're the one standing in front of me, so you'll do. The road runs west out of the Dry Hills and climbs into the mountains, and Sun Rock's the hold on the mesa. Put this in Envoy Garnak's hand and nobody else's.
st_road_west.accept_text: Don't stop at the Barrens' water holes on the way. They've been bad lately.

st_rot_in_the_heartwood.description: The Eldest Sequoia is the greatest tree on Stonetalon, and it's dying from the inside. The Venture Co. bored into it to tap its sap, and the heartrot beetles followed them in. Their queen is eating the tree's heart, and I can feel it every time I put my hand on the bark. The Eldest stands on the slopes of Stonetalon West, and you go in at its foot and climb. Kill the Heartrot Queen before there's nothing left to save.
st_rot_in_the_heartwood.accept_text: Go in at the Eldest Sequoia's foot in Stonetalon West. The queen nests in the chewed galleries. Bring friends along.

st_samples_from_the_rim.description: I know the tauren don't want me on Sun Rock, and I don't blame them. But whatever is getting the dead up in Mulgore isn't the Scourge, and it isn't anything the Forsaken have ever seen. I want to know what's doing it before it reaches anywhere else. I need tissue samples from the risen tauren and the risen stalkers on the Rim, in the south-east. The jars seal themselves, mostly, but I wouldn't count on it.
st_samples_from_the_rim.accept_text: Seal the jars by hand anyway. Mostly isn't good enough for this.
st_samples_from_the_rim.turn_in_text:
It's fascinating, and it's horrible. There's no plague in this tissue at all. Nothing I know of is holding it together.

Whatever's doing this isn't from Azeroth. I'd stake what's left of my life on it.

st_sap_on_the_slopes.description: The sap oozes are what happens when a sequoia bleeds. The Venture Co. taps the giants, the sap runs out, and then it gets up and walks away. It sticks to everything, and it sticks to my climbing rope worst of all. I can't climb with a rope full of sap. Clear them off the Sequoia Slopes so I can get up there.
st_sap_on_the_slopes.accept_text: The sap oozes crawl all over the Sequoia Slopes. Watch your feet.
st_sap_on_the_slopes.turn_in_text:
My rope's clean and so is the bark, so I can climb.

I'll take a look at the crown from up there and see what the eagles think of all this.

st_saw_boss_brakka.description: Saw-Boss Brakka runs the Venture Cutline. She was my foreman, and she's the one who decided the living giants were fair game. She won't stop while she's alive, I know her too well for that. I want her stopped, and every one of her foremen with her. She carries a saw on a pole that'll take your arm off, so go together.
st_saw_boss_brakka.accept_text: Stay out of reach of that pole. She swings it wide, and she doesn't tire.
st_saw_boss_brakka.turn_in_text:
Is she really down?

Then the Cutline's finished. The Cartel will buy what's left and turn it into something useful. Maybe they'll make it a sawmill for fallen wood. I'd like that.

st_shredder_gears.description: The Venture Co.'s shredder walkers do the work of ten crews each. I helped build the first ones, and I know they can't run without their drive gears, so pull the gears and the shredders are scrap. Before the Integration there were no trees this big to cut, and nobody would ever have built a machine this stupid to cut them. The shredders work the Venture Cutline. Bring me their gears, and don't climb into one while it's running.
st_shredder_gears.accept_text: Leave the grease on the gears. It tells me how hard they've been run.

st_skyreach.description: I got halfway up a sequoia before a sky serpent the size of a canoe came round the trunk at me. The ridge eagles used to nest up on the peak, and the biggest of the serpents, Skyreach, has been driving them off and taking their nests. I'd like to climb without being eaten. I'd also like the eagles to have their peak back. Skyreach hunts round Stonetalon Peak, and it'll come to you.
st_skyreach.accept_text: Leave the eagle chicks if you find any. They'll need the peak back more than anyone.

st_splintertree_answer.description: I've written back to Garnak. Splintertree can't spare warriors, not with the demons loose in Ashenvale, but I can spare arrows and a promise, and I've sent both. I want the answer carried back the way his report came, on foot. Tell him the arrows follow on the next cart. Tell him I meant the promise, and he'll know what I mean.
st_splintertree_answer.accept_text: Keep the promise part out of earshot of the crossroads. Not everyone needs to hear it.
st_splintertree_answer.turn_in_text:
Gorada doesn't hand out arrows or promises lightly, and she's sent both.

Kuna will want to know that Ashenvale's answered. Go and tell her.

st_sulphur_and_ash.description: I came to Stonetalon for the volcano's ash. Undercity's alchemists want it for something I won't explain, and the best ash on the mountain is the ash that walks around on its own: the crater ash wraiths on the peak. Stonetalon Peak is north of here, at the top of the mountain, where the wraiths drift round the rim and the Basalt Hulk brutes stamp round the crater. Bring me the ash, and keep the hulks off my sampling sites while you're up there. I'd do it myself if I'd ever been any use with anything sharper than a spatula.
st_sulphur_and_ash.accept_text: Seal the pouch tight. Ash that's walked around on its own gets out of things.
st_sulphur_and_ash.turn_in_text:
That's good, fine ash, and it's still trying to go back to the crater. Undercity will be delighted.

I won't say what for. You wouldn't sleep.

st_talondeep.description: I need a pair of eyes in Stonetalon. Orgrimmar's envoy at Sun Rock Retreat writes to me every week, and every week his letters get shorter. Either he's busy, or something's wrong, and I'd like to know which. The Talondeep Path runs south out of Ashenvale, through the hill and down onto a mountainside that used to be forest. Take him this letter and find out what's going on.
st_talondeep.accept_text: South down the Talondeep road, through the tunnel. Sun Rock's the big mesa in the middle of the burn.

st_taurajo_answer.description: I've read Muhana's letter twice, and I've written back. I'd like you to carry it, because I'd rather it went with someone who's seen Sun Rock with their own eyes. There's something I haven't written down, and I want you to tell her in person. Taurajo can't send her warriors. We have the Barrens to hold, and I'm sorry for it.
st_taurajo_answer.accept_text: Take it to Muhana. Tell her I'd come myself if the camp could spare me, and tell her it can't.

st_the_ancients_wake.description: Some of the giants were awake when they came through. I call them the Redwood Ancients, and since the Venture Co. started cutting, they've been waking in a rage and walking the vale, flattening anything they find. I've tried to calm them, and they won't listen to me any more. I need them put back to sleep the only way that works now. They walk in Greatwood Vale and on the Sequoia Slopes.
st_the_ancients_wake.accept_text: Don't stand still in front of one. They're slow to turn, and that's your only chance.

st_the_ash_mother.description: The ash wraiths come from somewhere, and I've found where. There's a hollow off the skylight in the Ashvent, where ash falls in through the roof and something gathers it into the shape of a woman. The ash mother makes the wraiths, and she's making more every week. I want her ash, all of it, preferably. The Ashvent opens on the peak's north flank, and she's in the hollow off the skylight.
st_the_ash_mother.accept_text: Go down the Ashvent to the skylight and find the hollow off it. Take friends who can stand the heat.
st_the_ash_mother.turn_in_text:
This is the ash of the thing that makes the ash. Undercity will want to talk to you.

They won't, of course. But I'll tell them you were extraordinary.

st_the_cutline.description: I ran a Venture Co. saw crew for years, and I quit the day they started cutting the living giants. Now I work for the Cartel, undoing what I used to do. The Venture Cutline is eating into the redwoods from the east, and I know every crew on it by name. The fellers cut, and the riggers haul. I want both of them stopped.
st_the_cutline.accept_text: The Venture Cutline's east of the camp, where the trees stop and the stumps start.

st_the_grimtotem_line.description: The Grimtotem have built a compound south of the Blowdown, and it creeps closer to Sun Rock every month. They're testing us, sending raider bands and spearhunter packs out to see how far they get before the watch notices. I want them to learn that the watch always notices. Their compound is to the south, past the Standing Grove, and their patrols work the ground round it. Hit them there, before they reach the road.
st_the_grimtotem_line.accept_text: If you see a runner heading back to the compound, take him first.

st_the_risen_hunter.description: There's one of the risen who leads the rest, and I knew him. He was a Bloodhoof hunter, the best tracker in Mulgore, and now he tracks for whatever's down there. I wouldn't send anyone after him until I knew Sun Rock wasn't standing alone. Camp Taurajo, Splintertree and the Aspen have all answered now, so it's time. He hunts the Mulgore Rim with the risen behind him, and he'll know you're coming.
st_the_risen_hunter.accept_text: Go together, and don't follow him past the Rim.

st_the_road_to_desolace.description: There's a road off the west side of Stonetalon that goes down toward Desolace. Iyana says nobody's come up it since the Integration, and nobody who's gone down has come back. I climb the redwoods over that road, and I want to know if it's still shut, and what's been coming up to the edge of it. The road's in the far south-west of Stonetalon West, past the vale, and the Fog Cougar packs hunt along it, so clear them on the way. Look down it, and come back and tell me what you saw.
st_the_road_to_desolace.accept_text: Take a rope in case the edge crumbles. I'd like you to come back up whatever you find.

st_the_salvage_yard.description: I'd like everybody to know the Steamwheedle Cartel has nothing to do with the Venture Co. The Venture Co. has set up a salvage yard in the middle of the Blowdown, stripping the dead forest for timber and selling it cheap, and it's ruining prices and the good name of goblins. I blame the newcomers a bit as well, because before the Integration nobody had heard of a whole forest just falling over. The Venture Salvage Yard is out on the Blowdown, north-west of here, and you can't miss it, because it's the only thing out there making noise. The Venture Co. Salvager crews and Bucker crews do the cutting, so stop them cutting.
st_the_salvage_yard.accept_text: If you find any of their price lists, bring them. I'd love to know how low they're going.

st_topping_the_eldest.description: The work order was real. The Venture Co. means to cut the Eldest Sequoia from the inside and the top at once. Rigboss Gazzle runs the crews climbing the trunk, and Topper Kezzik has a walking shredder up in the crown, cutting the top off so the rest comes down in pieces. I trained half those crews myself, which makes it my job to stop them, and since I'm no good in a fight, it's yours. Go into the Eldest Sequoia from the door at its foot, on the slopes north-east of here, and stop Gazzle inside the trunk and Kezzik up on the crown.
st_topping_the_eldest.accept_text: Bring a full crew, I mean it. Those rigs weren't built to be gentle.

st_vents_on_the_peak.description: The peak of Stonetalon is in the West, past the redwoods, and I'm convinced the vents up there are opening. Every Vent Steamling on that peak is really a vent walking around, a crack in the mountain letting off pressure. I want them put out, and I want someone to look into the crater from the rim. Take the road through Stonetalon West and up to the top. Tell me if the crater lake is steaming.
st_vents_on_the_peak.accept_text: Don't stand downwind of the crater. The steam burns before you feel it.
st_vents_on_the_peak.turn_in_text:
It's steaming, and the colour's changed. That's gas coming up through the water.

It's not going to blow tomorrow. But there's a lava tube on the flank that's feeding it, and something down there keeps it hot.

st_voss_replies.description: I've had Merrow's samples for a day and a night. What lives in the Arathi mere isn't the same thing as what's on his Rim, but it was made the same way, by something that doesn't need plague to hold the dead together. I've written it all down for him. My hand is small, so he'll need his spectacles. Take it back to Sun Rock for me.
st_voss_replies.accept_text: Take this back to Merrow at Sun Rock. Tell him he was right, and that I hate that he's right.
st_voss_replies.turn_in_text:
That's two places a world apart, with the same hand behind both.

I'll write to the Society, and they'll laugh. Then the third place will happen, and they'll stop laughing.

st_weezels_findings.description: I found the signature in the ledgers. The caps were signed out by a Krizzle, a Cartel man in Ratchet, on the very day he resigned. He took a key, a crate and the Cartel's good name with him, and the Cartel would like at least one of the three back. I've written it all up for Pixie Brightcog at Sun Rock Retreat, with the seal that means she has the Cartel's leave to do whatever she likes about it. Take these to her for me.
st_weezels_findings.accept_text: Don't let anyone see the seal on the way. A seal like that tends to get people asking favours.

st_what_raised_them.description: I want to see what the risen see. There's a cairn at the edge of the Mulgore Rim, south of here, right where the dark begins, and I believe the thing that raises them reaches up out of Mulgore there. I'd like you to stand at that cairn and tell me what you feel. Thin out the risen guarding it first, or you won't be standing long. Stay as long as you can bear it, and then come back and tell me everything.
st_what_raised_them.accept_text: Take something warm to hold. The cold up there gets in where you can't rub it out.
st_what_raised_them.turn_in_text:
You felt cold, and a pull downward, as if the ground wanted you. That's exactly what I felt, through the jars.

I'll write this up for the Royal Apothecary Society. They won't believe me either.

st_what_walks_the_rim.description: Every night more of them stand on the Rim and look toward Sun Rock. They were tauren once, and some of them were people I knew. Something in Mulgore killed them and then got them back up again, and now they hunt along the edge of the dark. I want the risen cut down, and I want the Rim looked at properly, from the overlook at the far end. Look, then come back and tell me what you saw, and don't stay too long.
st_what_walks_the_rim.accept_text: The risen walk the Mulgore Rim. The overlook is at the far end, where the ground drops into the dark.

st_wind_witch_fetishes.description: The wind witches are what keep the harpies coming. I've watched them through my glass, and before every raid they hold up little bundles of feather and bone, and the wind turns their way. I want those fetishes, so Spiritwalker Tohana can find out what they do and how to stop them. The witches stay near the top of Windshear Crag, north of here. Don't hold one up into the wind yourself, whatever you do.
st_wind_witch_fetishes.accept_text: Carry them wrapped in something heavy. Even in a pack, they'll try to catch the wind.

st_windshear_mine.turn_in_text:
That's the end of the fake stamps in Ratchet. Pixie's cousin is going to buy her a drink for this.

You can have this from me, and Pixie says you can have the drink as well.

st_word_to_splintertree.description: I've written to Overseer Gorada at Splintertree Post about the ladders, the fire and Hargol. I won't trust it to a wind rider, because the harpies have been knocking them out of the sky. It has to go on foot, north up the Talondeep Path to Ashenvale and through the tunnel. Splintertree's the Horde post on the other side, and Gorada will be on the wall, because she always is. Put it in her hand and nobody else's.
st_word_to_splintertree.accept_text: Keep to the middle of the tunnel. The harpies nest in the mouth at the far end.
st_word_to_splintertree.turn_in_text:
Siege ladders, fire, and a Grimtotem chief who thought he could have Sun Rock, and Garnak sends it on foot.

He was right to. I'll answer him now.

st_word_to_taurajo.description: Elder Longtread at Camp Taurajo speaks for the tauren now, while nobody knows where Cairne is. I've written to him about the Rim, about the refugees here, and about the dead that won't lie down on the Mulgore side. These are things I won't trust to a messenger who hasn't seen them. Camp Taurajo's in the southern Barrens, and the wind riders will take you most of the way. Put this in his hand, and tell me what he says.
st_word_to_taurajo.accept_text: Don't let anyone else read it, and don't read it yourself.

st_yard_boss_krizzle.description: Yard Boss Krizzle runs that salvage yard, and I've found out he used to be Cartel. He walked out with a warehouse key and a crate of our caps the day the Venture Co. offered him more money. Nobody steals from the Cartel and gets to keep the profit. He's in the middle of the Venture Salvage Yard, north-west of here, shouting at people. Deal with him, and make sure he knows it came from me.
st_yard_boss_krizzle.accept_text: If he offers you a cut to walk away, remember the number. I'd like to know what he thinks I'm worth.
